title: CLCON/333/2020 of PANKAJ KUMAR BANSAL Vs C RAVI SHANKAR

paras.text:
CLCON No.333 of 2020
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(via Video Conferencing)
Mr. Arvind Kumar Sharma, Advocate for the
petitioner.
The petitioner has filed this contempt petition
alleging non-compliance of the judgment of the
Division Bench dated 13.06.2018; as rendered in Writ
Petition (PIL) No.65 of 2011, Kunwar Pal Singh vs.
State of Uttarakhand and others.
In a nut shell, if the pleadings in para 9 of the
contempt petition is taken into consideration, the
dispute pertains to a "banjar land" recorded in Khasra
No.170 M, having an area of 0.03348 hectares situated
in Village Salempur Bukkal Pargana Manglor Tehsil,
Laksar, District Haridwar. He alleges that there is an
act of encroachment which has not been taken care of
by the respondents despite of the judgment of Division
Bench dated 13.06.2018. The record further revealed
that in relation to the land in question there had been a
proceedings under Section 122-B of the Zamindari
Abolition & Land Reforms Act, 1950 (hereinafter
referred to as the ZA & LR Act) which was decided on
23.07.1999 as against the alleged encroachers. There is
nothing on record to show that as against the said
judgment dated 23.07.1999; whether any subsequent
proceeding were drawn before the superior court and as
to whether it is the pending consideration or decided or
not till date.
In that view of the matter, since the issue
pertaining to the land in question was a subject matter
of 122-B proceedings provided under the provisions of
the ZA & LR Act, coupled with the fact that since the
dispute pertains to the "banjar land", which was not the
nature of land which was the subject matter of the PIL,
because the PIL related to johar, ponds, water bodies,
common grazing land. The implications of the Division
Bench judgment will not be attracted in the present
case, apart from it, the enforcement of judgment sought
by the present contempt petition, which has been

preferred before the Registry on 02.09.2020 seeking
enforcement of the judgment dated 13.06.2018 will
otherwise be barred by Section 20 of the Contempt of
Courts Act.
In view of the aforesaid, I am of the view that
this contempt petition is not tenable and accordingly
the same is dismissed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 15.09.2020
